The issue was resolved by applying a new `RoleBinding` (`config-reader-binding`) in the `default` namespace. This binding connects the `config-reader` ServiceAccount to the existing `Role` (`app-config-reader`), which grants `get` access solely to `configmaps/app-config`, thus maintaining least-privilege access. The unhealthy pod was deleted to force a restart, which successfully picked up the new permissions.

**Observed Change:**
A `RoleBinding` named `config-reader-binding` was created in the `default` namespace, binding the `ServiceAccount` `config-reader` to the `Role` `app-config-reader`.

**Verified Outcome:**
The original symptom is resolved. The deployment `app` now has all replicas healthy, as confirmed by the following observation:
```
NAME                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
app-5b674c446f-7v7fv   1/1     Running   0          43s
app-5b674c446f-djsz2   1/1     Running   0          42s
app-5b674c446f-hbt58   1/1     Running   0          19s
```
All application pods are now `1/1` Ready and `Running`.
message.reasoning_content:
All three replicas of the `app` deployment are now running and `1/1` Ready. This indicates that the newly created pod (or the pod replacing the failed one) successfully completed its initialization sequence. The error caused by missing RBAC has been resolved.

The original symptom was an "in-cluster configuration reader is unhealthy."
The evidence shows:
1. The previously failing pod `app-5b674c446f-kvz5j` (which had `0/1` readiness and `Init:Error`) is gone.
2. All pods in the deployment `app` are now `1/1` Ready and `Running`.

The configuration reader is healthy. I have restored it while preserving least-privilege access by adding only the necessary `RoleBinding` without altering the existing minimal `Role` definition.

I will now report the change and the verified outcome.
